friction: In three saved-file-passing curve-network-joining sessions, agents attempted update_object_attributes with destination layer Joined before creating that layer, each costing a failed call and, where retried, an additional call. The current tool description says the destination layer is optional but does not state that a supplied layer name/full path must already exist or point agents to create_layer.
evidence: Three underlying update_object_attributes failures explicitly reported that layer Joined was not found: one baseline and two candidate sessions in curve-network-joining.

The audit records three missing-object-classified update_object_attributes failures and three same-intent retries; supervisor review identifies the classifier label as instrumentation noise, not a missing-object/plugin conclusion.
All affected task verdicts passed, so this is workflow inefficiency/recovery friction rather than evidence of correctness failure.
The 13 host execution refusals are gateway restrictions, not evidence for this proposal.
hypothesis: A description-only clarification that destination_layer must already exist, with create_layer as the prerequisite, will reduce premature layer-assignment failures and recovery calls without changing update_object_attributes behavior or task correctness. This remains unmeasured until a pinned AB/BA evaluation.
preserve: Change only the update_object_attributes MCP tool description/docstring; no executable AST, schema, command behavior, other tool descriptions, plugin bytes, model recipe, task prompt, evaluator, budget, or environment changes.
Use fixed gpt-5.6-terra medium, 50 calls, 240 seconds, full catalog, and refused host execution for baseline/candidate AB/BA comparisons.
Require all saved-file tasks to pass, no per-task task-success or failed-call regression, and no adoption without measured benefit in at least one discovery family.
Treat small-assemblies and directional-curve-projection as planned validation only; directional-curve-projection is held out from the supplied audit.
